title: String-based algorithm identification in UAPI — no integer IDs or enums
description: All algorithm and provider identification in the UAPI uses null-terminated strings (algo[], provider[] in every ioctl struct), not integer IDs or enum values. This is correct for ABI stability: integer IDs require both kernel and userspace to be recompiled when a new algorithm is added, because the ID table is a shared closed universe. String names are an open namespace — a new algorithm like 'hkdf(sha3-256)' is added to a provider, and userspace binaries compiled before that addition can request it by name without recompile. Integer ID schemes also require a central registry that becomes ABI debt. A reviewer might suggest 'use integer IDs for efficiency and easy validation' — that suggestion should be rejected: validation of a string is a strncmp, not slower than a range check, and the ABI consequence of integer IDs is permanent closed-universe breakage. This is the same reason Linux /proc/crypto uses strings, not IDs.
